subject: Recap & next steps: Stride trial success metrics and ops checklist
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria@stridehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps: Stride trial success metrics and ops checklist

Thanks again for the call earlier, Maria — good alignment on business goals and the three core workflows you want to validate (claims summarization, patient triage prompts, and internal search reranking). I wanted to capture the proposed success criteria and immediate next steps so we have a single place to iterate.

1) Trial scope and success criteria (proposal)
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 150 ms for short prompts (~64 tokens) and <= 350 ms for long prompts (~512 tokens) under your 50qps burst profile.
- Throughput: sustained throughput target of ~20 requests/sec (average request length ~200 tokens) on a single dedicated instance type (we'll size in the kickoff).
- Cost: target cost/token <= $0.0006 (aiming for $0.00045 with batching/quantization).
- Quality: automated eval pass rate >= 92% on the validation set (we'll define the pass metric per prompt type). Hallucination rate < 2% in factual extraction tasks.
- Stability: no more than 1% error responses (timeouts/5xx) during steady-state 24h window.

2) Evaluation plan (high level)
- You provide representative sample set (CSV) for the three workflows, annotated where available; Redwood will run baseline runs, synthetic stress tests, and a 72-hour smoke run.
- Metrics collection: token counts, per-request latency distributions, KV cache hit rates, and quality labels. We'll surface dashboards in the Console and provide a short report after the 72h run.

3) Ownership and timeline
- Action: Stride to share sample dataset + privacy checklist — owner: Maria — target: 2026-07-26.
- Action: Redwood to provision trial environment & smoke checklist — owner: Ben — target: 2026-07-27.
- Action: Kickoff run (72-hour smoke + baseline) — owners: Grace (ops lead) & Jordan (solutions eng) — window: 2026-07-28 to 2026-07-30.
- Action: Results review + decision gate (go/no-go for pilot expansion) — owner: Maria + Stride execs — target: 2026-07-31.

4) Risks and mitigation
- If throughput targets exceed a single instance, we will propose a small Dedicated pool with autoscaling; early tests will surface this.
- If quality below threshold, we'll run a focused prompt engineering loop and evaluate quantization/finer model selection.

Attachments: I attached a simple workload snapshot template (stride-workload-snapshot.csv) and the initial MPA draft for procurement (redwood-poc-mpa-draft.pdf).

Next steps: Maria, please confirm the dataset delivery date and whether the sample contains any PHI (if so, we'll enable the Private onboarding checklist). I'll schedule a short kickoff slot for Tue 7/28 09:00-10:00 PT unless you prefer another time.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications and commitments:

- We can deliver a 2k-row sample CSV for each workflow by Monday 7/26 evening PST. The files will be scrubbed but may contain pseudonymized PHI fields — we will flag those.
- On quality: the 92% pass rate sounds reasonable as a starting gate for the summarization task; for reranking, we care more about top-1 precision improving vs current baseline by >= 8 points.
- Latency: our internal SLO target is 200ms p95 for the triage prompts; we understand there are different buckets and are OK splitting the definition by short vs long.

We confirm the 7/28 kickoff window; Alex will be the internal product lead for the trial and will join the review. Procurement will need the MPA; forwarding to procurement now.

Looping back with an ops-focused checklist I will follow during provisioning and the smoke run. Ben — feel free to paste this into the Drive doc so Maria's team sees it.

Provisioning checklist (Grace — owner)
- Create dedicated trial env in us-west-2 (VPC, private control plane)
- Provision 1 x c5g-dedicated inference instance (baseline), attach monitoring hooks, enable Console telemetry
- Preload KV-cache where relevant for reranking workflows
- Load dataset into staging (ensure pseudonymized markers preserved), run data validation tests
- Prepare Canary traffic generator: 1qps -> 10qps -> 50qps ramp over 30 mins for smoke test

Metric collection plan
- Capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens-per-second, model selection logs, batch sizes, and error rates
- Export results to shared Drive + add a short README with evaluation snippets

Acceptance gating for go/no-go
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for triage (short prompts), p95 <= 350ms for long prompts
- Quality: summarization pass >= 90% (we'll reconcile exact annotation rubric with Stride)
- Stability: error rate < 1.5% during the 72h window

I will start the provision on 7/27 evening and aim to have the environment ready for the 7/28 kickoff. Attaching the provisioning playbook and the workload template to the Drive folder.

Grace O'Connor
